newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislature recesses, budget deal elusive.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislature recesses, budget deal elusive.

text.p: Both houses of the California legislature recessed on Thursday for the weekend with little hope of passing a budget before the start of the 1997-1998 fiscal year on July 1.
Leaders of the state Senate and Assembly and the state's budget conference committee said the major stumbling block in talks was welfare reform.
"It's a retooling of the entire welfare system. We ought to do it comprehensively," Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, told reporters after the session ended.
He told the Senate to be prepared to meet over the July 4 holiday weekend. "We're moving closer to a closing phase," he said.
The legislature's budget conference committee -- made up of three senators and three assembly members -- has been holding daily hearings on the state's key fiscal issues.

The committee's goal was to meld the budget packages of the state Assembly and Senate into a single spending plan for the fiscal year that begins July 1. The committee has already missed the state's Constitutional budget deadline of June 15.
The final budget was expected to be in the $67 billion to $70 billion range.
